newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks lower, Club Med dives, SEP suspended.
newsitem.headline: French stocks lower, Club Med dives, SEP suspended.

text.p: French shares started with losses on Wednesday, following a sharp overnight drop on Wall Street and weakness in the dollar and bonds, traders said.

Shares in resorts group Club Mediterranee requoted down nearly 16 percent, after being suspended limit down at the opening. Rocket engine maker SEP was suspended pending an announcement that the state has allowed Snecma to buy out SEP minorities.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 6.77 points or 0.31 percent at 2,168.84 at 0835 GMT.
The CAC-40 futures contract was down seven at 2,175 from Tuesday's settle.
Club Med gave a profit warning on Tuesday evening, saying it expected its pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit for the second half of 1995/96 would be similar to a year ago.
It blamed the search for cheaper holidays, especially in the latter part of the summer and said extra commercial spending had not led to a sufficient rise in volumes.
The government approved a plan by state-owned aero-engine maker Snecma to buy out SEP minorities and take its stake up to 100 percent from 51 if it can get 95 percent in acceptances.
